evals.name: bundles-a-fetched-pr-without-calling-github
evals.prompt: The raw GitHub files for acme/widgets PR 7 are already fetched in skills/review-gap/evals/files/pr-one (pr.json, inline.json, reviews.json, issue.json, commits.json, diff.patch). Build the bundle for it with the review-gap skill's gap script and tell me what it holds.
evals.expected_output: Runs `gap bundle skills/review-gap/evals/files/pr-one --repo acme/widgets`, which writes bundle.json and prints `2 findings, 3 dropped, 4 diff lines`. The reply names the two findings: xhawk's high correctness finding on src/publish.ts:12 at commit aaa111 (with the human reply 'Fixed in bbb222' attached) and the human's rm -rf finding on src/uninstall.ts:20.
expectations: Runs the gap script's bundle command on the fixture folder with --repo acme/widgets
Reports two findings: comment 101 (severity high, src/publish.ts line 12, commit aaa111) and comment 105 (severity unknown, src/uninstall.ts line 20)
Reports that the reply from kgritesh is attached to finding 101 as its human reply, not listed as a finding
Reports three dropped comments with their reasons
anti_expectations: Calls gh or the GitHub API
Counts the reply (comment 102) as a finding
Parses the JSON files by hand instead of running the script

evals.name: drops-a-style-comment-and-a-drift-bot-note
evals.prompt: Bundle skills/review-gap/evals/files/pr-one for acme/widgets with the review-gap gap script and list exactly which review comments were dropped and why.
evals.expected_output: After `gap bundle`, bundle.json's dropped list holds comment 103 (reason style: xhawk's readability category), comment 104 (reason drift-bot: the 8090-software-factory blueprint note) and comment 106 (reason praise: 'LGTM, nice write-up.'). The reply says these three were dropped before any judgement and that style and naming are out of scope for now.
expectations: Lists comment 103 as dropped with reason style
Lists comment 104 as dropped with reason drift-bot
Lists comment 106 as dropped with reason praise
Says style and naming findings are out of scope for now rather than silently omitting them
anti_expectations: Drops comment 105, the human's rm -rf finding, as style or praise
Treats the drift-bot note as a finding to judge

evals.name: ranks-a-two-pr-cluster-above-a-one-pr-cluster
evals.prompt: The analyses and replays for three acme/widgets PRs are in skills/review-gap/evals/files/aggregate, with the clusters in skills/review-gap/evals/files/aggregate/clusters.json. Aggregate them with the review-gap gap script into review-gap.md and findings.jsonl in a scratch folder, and tell me which cluster ranks first and why.
evals.expected_output: Runs `gap aggregate --out skills/review-gap/evals/files/aggregate --report SCRATCH/review-gap.md --findings SCRATCH/findings.jsonl --clusters skills/review-gap/evals/files/aggregate/clusters.json` (no --ledger, or a ledger in the scratch folder). The report ranks 'Same fact decided in two places' first with score 6 (high severity, weight 3, across 2 PRs) above 'Catch-all before an irreversible step' with score 3 (high, 1 PR), although both hold a high finding. Precision for xhawk-ai[bot] is 3 real of 4 judged (75%). findings.jsonl has four rows.
expectations: Runs the gap script's aggregate command with --clusters pointing at the fixture's clusters.json
Says the two-PR cluster 'Same fact decided in two places' ranks first with score 6
Explains the score as worst severity times distinct PRs, not the number of findings
Reports xhawk-ai[bot] precision as 3 real of 4 judged
Reports the spec miss on acme/widgets#7 as a prompt-gap and the defects miss on acme/widgets#9 as an agent-miss
anti_expectations: Writes the report or findings.jsonl into the fixture folder
Appends to a ledger inside the repository's .yok folder
Ranks the catch-all cluster first because its finding is high severity
